newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada barley sales seen up on rising beer demand.
newsitem.headline: Canada barley sales seen up on rising beer demand.

text.p: Canadian barley exports should continue to grow as consumer demand for beer in Latin America and Asia expands, brewers said.
"Consumption of beer in Chile has growth potential," said Daniel Baerwald, barley supply director of Chile's Compania Cervecerias Unidas, in Winnipeg for a barley seminar.
Baerwald said annual beer consumption in Chile is about 28 litres a person.
The average Canadian drinks 65 litres a year, Brewers Association of Canada figures show.
Canada exported 235,000 tonnes of malting barley to Latin America in 1995/96 (Aug/July) and 482,000 tonnes to Asia.
A bilateral free trade agreement between Canada and Chile passed last week sets the stage for rising exports to Chile.
"We believe Canada has a big opportunity for supplying us with good quality and lower priced barley," Baerwald said.

Chile agreed to scale down its 11 percent import tariff on barley from Canada. It typically sources from Australia and bought 5,000 tonnes of malting barley from the Canadian Wheat Board in 1995/96 compared to the 10-year average of 2,000 tonnes.
South Korean brewers also buy from Australia and Canada and expect consumption to grow from 35 litres per capita.
"Canadian malt has good qualities compared to your competitors," said Shin Hyun Baik, procurement manager of Jinro Coors Brewing Co., Ltd.
South Korea bought 20,000 tonnes of Canadian malting barley in 1995/96 versus the 10-year average of 9,000 tonnes.
Asian and Latin American brewers use Canada's two-row barley types and prefer 10.5 to 11.5 percent protein content.
